title: Studentized Inference for Quantiles under a Shrinking Dose-Window Intervention
banked_reason: D0.5 math/rubric PASS; general incremental, paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < field gate 7.4. Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded; independent validity consult concurs.
gap_reasons: The 0.8207 coverage calculation concerns this estimator at critical rank, and the proved smaller-rank regime permits linear calibration, so it establishes neither class-wide necessity of quadratic studentization nor a necessary lower rank boundary
The delivered scope remains one scalar quantile with fixed bandwidth and smoothness specifications; the proposed two-window contrast and the lottery application receive no inference theorem

The projected score is constrained by this restricted theoretical reach and the absence of reproducible performance evidence for the retuned procedure, whose slow certification rates leave moderate-sample calibration unresolved; no stale minimax or sharpness claim was identified in the framing
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery discharged the feasible shrinking-window quantile procedure, fitted-score replacement, measurable root inversion, full variance consistency, and coverage; a maximality pass added a rank elbow, a lower-rank linear-studentization law, and optimized pilot rates. Math and rubric reviews passed, but the final contribution was graded incremental (score ceiling 6.1 versus field floor 7.4), and an independent validity consult found no bounded within-scope repair. The reviewed derivation is preserved for a materially expanded re-anchor; Lean formalization, class-wide necessity, joint contrast inference, application inference, and reproducible moderate-sample evidence were not delivered.
tldr: The exact quantile \(q_h\) of a known shrinking dose-window intervention admits a total four-block quadratic estimating equation with learned projection geometry and data-only variance calibration on the fixed rough-covariate primitive class. At \(k\asymp nh\), both Hoeffding components contribute, and the full studentizer gives uniform Gaussian inference and asymptotic \(90\)-percent Wald coverage. The indexed fitted-score replacement, local inversion, pilot and Gram certification, validation, and root measurability are proved; the early kill test is discharged. Retuned pilots give a centered replacement factor \(n^{-1/8}\sqrt{\log(en)}\) at critical rank. The sufficient rank interval \(n^{5/8}L_n\leq k\leq nh\), \(L_n\to\infty\), also supports linear-only calibration when \(k/(nh)\to0\). Omitting quadratic variance at critical rank instead gives the explicit interior-submodel coverage loss. These are results for the declared procedure and class, not minimax necessity.
gap: Existing higher-order implicit theory credits localized rate control, and small-bandwidth theory credits Gaussian limits with competing Hoeffding terms. Neither result, as verified here, certifies the complete nested-pilot, learned-Gram, signed-root procedure on the stated rough covariate class.
fill: The central proposed result couples primitive pilot and density certification, learned projection geometry, indexed score replacement, root measurability, and validation estimation of both finite-cell variance components. The first unresolved step remains visible and may refute the proposed construction.
